threads.body: `register_post_import_hook` is used to defer wrapping, but the hook is never removed/disabled on `uninstrument()`. If Agno submodules (e.g. `agno.workflow.workflow`, `agno.knowledge.knowledge`) are imported after `AgnoInstrumentor().uninstrument()`, the post-import hook will still run and re-patch methods, effectively re-enabling instrumentation unexpectedly (and can also stack multiple wrappers across instrument/uninstrument cycles).

+def _safe_wrap_function(
+    target_module: str,
+    target_name: str,
+    wrapper: Callable[..., Any],
+) -> None:
+    """Safely wrap a method if it exists, deferring if module is not yet imported."""
+
+    def _apply(mod: Any) -> None:
+        try:
+            parts = target_name.split(".")
+            curr = mod
+            for part in parts:
+                curr = getattr(curr, part)
+        except AttributeError:
+            # Target class or method may not exist across all supported Agno versions.
+            return
+        wrap_function_wrapper(mod, target_name, wrapper)
+
+    if target_module in sys.modules:
+        _apply(sys.modules[target_module])
+        return
+
+    # Defer wrapping to avoid eagerly importing submodules with heavy or optional dependencies.
+    register_post_import_hook(_apply, target_module)

Great point.. I ended up creating new classes `SyncToolStreamWrapper` and `AsyncToolStreamWrapper` in utils to handle this case but it is tricky. 

Check out commit [8a15a66](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-genai/pull/673/commits/8a15a66161fc1cd95ba93170e07a25881b14c8d6)

In Agno, synchronous streaming tools execute sequentially and are iterated to completion on the same thread. In async runs, tools execute concurrently in separate tasks/threads; because context is copied upon creation, each tool correctly inherits the parent context and is recorded as a sibling span.

But these classes don't work well if someone calls `next` just once on the iterator/generator and then leaves the stream for a while and comes back later (be cause the tool call will be the parent span in the context).. It's hard to design this without knowing exactly what the use case is though.. Agno is the only one doing this right now..

I also directly access `GenAiInvocation._context_token` inside the stream wrapper classes, maybe theres a better way to do that..

Maybe we should not attach context at all for streaming tools? Yes, correlation with child spans created inside the generator might be lost, but leaking context is not great.

`_activate_context()` leaks the tool span into the caller thread during iteration, between chunks, or if iteration breaks early. Here is a test showing the leak:

```python
def test_tool_stream_partial_iteration_restores_caller_context(instrument_agno) -> None:
    from collections.abc import Iterator
    from opentelemetry.trace import get_current_span

    def streaming_tool() -> Iterator[str]:
        yield "chunk1"
        yield "chunk2"

    caller = get_current_span()
    call = FunctionCall(
        function=Function.from_callable(streaming_tool), arguments={}
    )
    result = call.execute()
    it = iter(result.result)
    assert next(it) == "chunk1"
    assert get_current_span() is caller
```

If you want to try to prevent leaks, you can use the `.context` property on the invocation instead of private `_context_token` - just added in one of the recent PRs.
I added a `suspend` method and `activate` contextmanager to the base GenAIInvocation  so that we can wrap all the streaming tool methods and toggle the context on and off.. let me know what you think

+    def suspend(self) -> None:
+        """Restore the context that was current before this invocation started.
+
+        Call this when handing control back to the caller while the invocation
+        is still running -- returning a stream the caller has not drained yet,
+        for example -- so unrelated caller work is not parented under this
+        invocation's span. Idempotent, and pairs with ``activate``.

+        if token is not None:
+            detach(token)

+    @contextmanager
+    def activate(self) -> Iterator[None]:
+        """Make this invocation's span the current span inside the block.
+
+        Restores the previous context on exit. A no-op when the span is
+        already current, so a nested block leaves the outermost one to restore
+        it, and a no-op once the invocation has finished.

+class SyncToolStreamWrapper(SyncStreamWrapper[ChunkT]):
+    """Stream wrapper for synchronous tool executions that return iterators/generators.
+
+    Tool executions return an iterator or generator to the caller before it is
+    drained. This wrapper restores the caller's context before returning, and
+    makes the tool span current only while tool code runs -- producing a chunk,
+    closing, or finalizing -- so caller work between chunks is not parented
+    under the tool. Per-chunk content is accumulated and set on
+    ``invocation.tool_result`` upon completion.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        stream: _SyncStream[ChunkT],
+        invocation: ToolInvocation,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(stream)
+        self._self_tool_invocation = invocation
+        invocation.suspend()
+        self._self_chunks: list[Any] = []
